title: Q-RES-ashby-journal-J1: Many parts adapting on one shared setting at once (measured 0.466, target <= 0)
body:
**Owner:** product-manager
**Trigger:** research pass: ashby-journal finding J1 is not-met (measured 0.466)
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation research --probe ashby-journal:J1
**Prediction:** second_loop_collision_share_7d <= 0 within 168 h
**Out of scope:** editing the study, its target or the paper to match the code; the measurement is changed only by changing the mechanism
**Closing probe:** `python3 -m foundation research --probe ashby-journal:J1`
**Status:** closed

Concern: Many parts adapting on one shared setting at once. The study: Ashby: parts of a multistable system can adapt simultaneously provided channel width is adequate and a disperser is provided (p. 4641); separate clusters adapt in the way that gives minimal interaction (p. 4178); trials within a larger trial only if functionally disconnected while they run (p. 4547). Two variables trying changes on the same step-function at once each judge the other's change as their own.

Mechanisms that should answer it: MULTISTABLE-1 (foundation/ultrastability.py).

Metric: share of the second loop's parameter steps in the last 7 days that changed a step-function another variable's trial already held (MULTISTABLE-1), target <= 0. Improve the mechanism (or add one) until the probe passes; the white paper at /research updates itself from the same measurement.

**Disposition:** shelved (ttl, 2026-11-27T17:23:13Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** open 6.1 hours (limit 6 hours) and no loop closed it (SLA-8H-1). Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).
